Filename-derived display labels with capital-letter spacing

EXE: DWAgent-dynamic-10443-v6-x64.exe
Portal: https://82.25.46.70:10443/
Config: os_win_installer/install-dynamic-10443-v6.json
SHA256: 8beb3ce0ff923b4ac157c2aa4120719ae230660669df7078502c560b6b481f61

Each installed process gets a friendly label from its own portal filename.
Remove a terminal .exe (case insensitive), then insert a space before every
capital after the first character unless whitespace is already present.
Examples:
  Main process filename RemoDwAgentAcess.exe -> Remo Dw Agent Acess
  Service process filename RemoDwAgentAcess.exe -> Remo Dw Agent Acess
  Service display name RemoDwAgent -> Remo Dw Agent
The formatted service display name controls Services and Control Panel.
Different main/service filenames produce separate friendly descriptions.
This is literal spacing: ABC.exe becomes A B C; no acronym grouping is applied.

Keep the portal values compact, as in those examples. Filenames, internal
Windows service identifiers, installation path, publisher and raw saved profiles
remain unchanged. Derived labels may grow to 199 characters without truncation.
Formatting mode is saved outside the raw profile and restored for uninstall
and replacement helpers so registration rollback keeps its proper display label.
Older v5 configuration retains its prior Service display name source behavior.

Custom names are fetched through the existing authenticated profile during setup.
No new portal field, server deployment or port change is required. Custom example
profile values are not included in the installer payload. Saving portal settings
affects new installs or verified replacements; existing installations need
reinstalling with this EXE. Windows controls Task Manager grouping; its Details
tab still shows actual executable filenames.

Only fresh copied executables are customized before startup. Resource writes use
private sibling staging and atomic replacement. Existing versions, copyright,
code, icons and manifests are preserved. As with v5, customized runtime copies
do not retain the original Python Authenticode signature. Publisher in Installed
Apps is separate from code signing/UAC publisher.

Validation: 129-test installer suite passed; the additional formatting-mode
persistence regression also passed, for 130 installer tests in total. All 16
portal identity/client-credential tests passed. The 15 process-description tests
include real Windows version.dll and .NET checks, exact requested examples,
different main/service names, long labels, legacy v5 behavior and failure cleanup.
Archive integrity, payload source/native equality, default-only configuration,
Python 3.8 syntax and preservation of all 73 pre-existing EXEs were verified.
Both modified binaries passed harmless execution checks on temporary copies.
No installed agent or live portal service was modified, started or stopped.
